corrections.source_says: The PDF includes Appendices A-D on pp. 25-29, explicitly referenced in Section 5. Set exists to yes and in_this_pdf to true; identify these appendices in where. They contain classifier implementation and validation, human calibration of similarity thresholds, bandit actions and rewards, and simulated evaluations. They do not supply participant-level standard errors for the main experimental contrasts. Appendix C also mentions Supplementary.C, without a separate usable link.
corrections.quote: We provide detailed technical descriptions of the methods and their evaluations in Appendix A and B.
corrections.locator: p. 9, Section 5; pp. 25-29, Appendices A-D; p. 27, Appendix C

corrections.form_value: Only S1, the randomized comparison of the two chatbot facilitators, is listed and summarized.
corrections.source_says: The paper explicitly reports a second study: an expert facilitated an hour-long workshop without chatbots and was then interviewed. The workshop is reported as having 11 participants, but the same passage gives 8 men and 4 women; flag this internal discrepancy rather than silently replacing the stated count. No random assignment to this human baseline is reported, and its participants must not be added to the randomized study to meet the sample-size threshold. Add the expert evaluation and its non-randomized baseline comparisons: notable-idea proportions are 0.66 (structured), 0.51 (adaptive), and 0.64 (human), with both chatbot-human comparisons p > 0.1; seed-similarity comparisons give p = 0.80 for structured versus human and p < 0.01 for adaptive versus human. This additional study does not involve generative-AI assistance.
corrections.quote: The workshop was held for an hour with 11 participants (Mean age = 27.18, SD = 7.55, self-identified as men = 8 and women = 4)
corrections.locator: p. 3, study overview; p. 17, Section 8 Expert evaluation; p. 18, Fig. 11; p. 19, Section 9 identifies Study 1 and Study 2

corrections.form_value: Only S1 is listed; notes is empty.
corrections.source_says: The appendices also report technical evaluations that should be identified separately from the ideation experiment: classifier prediction and latency benchmarks in A.1-A.2, human threshold calibration in A.3, and a simulated bandit evaluation in D.1. The calibration uses 10 raters judging 84 pairs sampled from 100 prepared ideas; only the presentation order of pairs is randomized. These are raters, pairs, and prepared ideas, not additional people randomized to generative-AI-assisted creation. GPT-4 is used in the classifier benchmark, not as the assistance given to the ideators. The number of retained ratings after excluding neutral judgments is not stated and should remain null.
corrections.quote: 10 participants (Mean age = 24.80, SD = 4.26, 5 males) reviewed the selected pairs in a randomized order
corrections.locator: p. 25, Appendix A.1-A.2; p. 26, Appendix A.3, steps 1-4; pp. 28-29, Appendix D.1

corrections.form_value: Both outcomes: question = with_ai; ai_available_when_produced = yes; comparison_type = ai_design.
corrections.source_says: These codes should be none, no, and other, respectively, under the codebook definition of AI as generative AI. Both interventions retrieve other participants' ideas and supply predetermined facilitation actions using a fine-tuned DistilBERT similarity classifier and, for the adaptive facilitator, a bandit algorithm. The paper tested GPT-4 only in a preliminary classifier benchmark and chose DistilBERT for the deployed chatbots. The current outcome codes therefore conflict with the correctly excluded, non-generative intervention described elsewhere in the form.
corrections.quote: Accordingly, we conclude the fine-tuned classifier is more suited to our interaction scenario and used it for our chatbots.
corrections.locator: pp. 7-8, Section 4 and Fig. 4; p. 9, Section 5.1; p. 10, Fig. 5; p. 27, Appendix C

corrections.form_value: measure = embedding_similarity; measure_detail = an empty string.
corrections.source_says: Use automated_score and describe the fine-tuned DistilBERT semantic-textual-similarity prediction. The document describes a learned similarity score, with training on SemEval2017-STS using mean-squared-error loss; it does not identify an embedding-distance or cosine-similarity calculation for this outcome. Section 7.2.1 applies the predicted score to each idea against one fixed seed idea, rather than computing diversity across different participants' outputs.
corrections.quote: Internally, the fine-tuned classifier predicts a score on a 5-point scale.
corrections.locator: p. 9, Section 5.1; p. 13, Section 7.2.1; p. 25, Appendix A

corrections.source_says: Include test_statistic. The source reports mixed-ANOVA F statistics and p values, which are already transcribed correctly in reported: chatbot F(1, 358) = 60.93, p < 0.01; day F(1, 358) = 0.26, p = 0.61; interaction F(1, 358) = 6.01, p = 0.02. No standardized effect or confidence interval for this contrast is printed.
corrections.quote: there was a significant main effect of chatbot facilitators on the similarity of ideas

confirmed: Source version, title, and authors are correct: arXiv:2503.03617v1 [cs.HC], 5 Mar 2025; the local PDF has 29 pages and a manuscript DOI placeholder, not the ACM version of record (p. 1; final page 29). The entire markdown, including Appendices A-D, was read.

S1 is an online randomized experiment with individual assignment: 48 people recruited via social networks, 24 assigned to each facilitator, with gender balance considered (pp. 11-12, Section 6.2 and Fig. 6; p. 12, Section 6.5).
The recorded participant demographics match: mean age 27.21, SD 4.95, 21 men and 27 women (p. 11, Section 6.2).

The randomized study is below the 50-person threshold. The satisfaction results explicitly use 24 participants per group, but no separate participant analysis count is supplied for the idea-similarity ANOVA; leaving that analyzed count unconfirmed is appropriate, and its denominator degrees of freedom must not be treated as people (p. 11, Fig. 6; p. 13, Section 7.2.1; p. 15, Section 7.3.3).

Core = no, criterion 1 = not_met, criterion 2 = not_met, and context_class = none are supported: the randomized arms use non-generative facilitation, and the additional human workshop and calibration evaluation supply no randomized generative-AI assistance study (pp. 7-11, Sections 4-6; p. 17, Section 8; pp. 25-28, Appendices A-D).

The five-day task had two days of generation, two days of selection, and final review of three selected ideas; it concerned improving daily life during a pandemic (p. 11, Section 6 and Fig. 6; p. 12, Section 6.3).

Idea similarity is measured against the single seed, A clear mask that allows people to see your expressions. Structured mean 0.93 (SD = 0.4) and adaptive mean 1.41 (SD = 0.4) match the source; higher means more similar to the seed, not a direct across-people diversity score (p. 13, Section 7.2.1; p. 14, Fig. 9).
Every ANOVA number in S1-O1.reported matches: chatbot F(1, 358) = 60.93, p < 0.01; day F(1, 358) = 0.26, p = 0.61; chatbot-by-day F(1, 358) = 6.01, p = 0.02 (p. 13, Section 7.2.1).

Every count in S1-O2.reported matches: 474 structured-group ideas and 395 adaptive-group ideas; 311 and 200 ideas, respectively, retained for review after filtering. These are idea counts, not participant counts; no test of the raw generation totals is reported (p. 12, Section 7; p. 13, Fig. 7).
The one_line_finding accurately states the randomized sample, direction, similarity means, F statistic, p value, and idea totals (p. 11, Fig. 6; pp. 12-13, Sections 7 and 7.2.1).

Self-ratings of helpfulness, creativity-support and usability surveys, and satisfaction with selected ideas are described separately from the computed similarity outcome (p. 12, Section 6.4; pp. 14-15, Sections 7.2.2-7.3.3).

This is not a synthesis; the default null synthesis counts and absent pooled estimates are appropriate (pp. 9-18, Sections 5-8). The document identifies academic affiliations and public research support, and its promised code link is removed for anonymity (p. 1; p. 4, contribution 3 and footnote 1; p. 21, Acknowledgments).
summary: The 48-person randomized study used non-generative chatbot facilitators, so it does not qualify for the generative-AI pipeline; the recorded numerical findings match the PDF. Corrections concern omitted studies and appendices, generative-AI outcome labels, and measurement/statistics metadata.
